<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 79 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **58** of **210** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **175** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 421bb6b7973ad8823e2c953c9314b15dc0312237` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `7a6141956b35810497ef203b1167c9beb2651099` — the merge of head `b3d92fee1573d4f20f93de76b5344320e75bac4d` into base `421bb6b7973ad8823e2c953c9314b15dc0312237`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 7a6141956b35810497ef203b1167c9beb2651099 && git checkout 7a6141956b35810497ef203b1167c9beb2651099
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 421bb6b7973ad8823e2c953c9314b15dc0312237 b3d92fee1573d4f20f93de76b5344320e75bac4d && git checkout -B drift-repro 421bb6b7973ad8823e2c953c9314b15dc0312237 && git merge --no-ff b3d92fee1573d4f20f93de76b5344320e75bac4d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 421bb6b7973ad8823e2c953c9314b15dc0312237
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 421bb6b7973ad8823e2c953c9314b15dc0312237` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

- **Shape:** 23 files, +1127 / −45 at head `7237921e`. `disabledActions` beside `item` on `GetMetaItemResponseSchema` and `GetMetaItemCachedResponseSchema` (`string[]`), and a name-keyed sibling of `items` on `GetMetaItemsResponseSchema` (`Record<objectName, string[]>`), all optional (`packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts`). The seam is `IObjectQLEngine.getDisabledActions?(): string[] | undefined` (`packages/spec/src/contracts/objectql-engine.ts`), read by metadata-protocol through the service table by name (`protocol-action-activation-reads.ts`), never an `objectql` import. `describeDisabled()` (`packages/objectql/src/action-activation.ts`) is now "This action is turned off for this deployment. An administrator can turn it on again under Setup › Packaged automation, or you can use another action."; the code `ACTION_DISABLED` / 409 stay, and the ledger + ADR-0126 §8 go to the engine's log line. Changesets: spec minor, metadata-protocol / objectql / rest / runtime patch, `Clause-②: yes (widening)` / `Metadata-protocol: added`. Matches ruling 6512814276 (letter B) and triage 6513025554.
- **Measured choices (the card left them to the seat and its review):**
  - **Key name `disabledActions`** (the triage route's spelling). ⛔ Not final until the maintainer approves it in this PR (triage: "the maintainer approves the key in the PR").
  - **`[]` vs absent:** absent = no ledger answered (no engine member, or no store attached); `[]` = a ledger answered and none of this object's actions is off. Same split `registration` makes.
  - **ETag / 304:** out of the ETag, and a read carrying the key is never answered 304, the #23316 trade the card's "Wanted 1" names. **For the contract reviewer:** a ledger is attached on every `PlatformObjectsPlugin` boot, so on a default deployment every cached `GET /meta/object/:name` now answers 200, not 304. `registration` paid this only on flows; objects are the console's hottest metadata read. The alternative is to fold the switched-off names for this object into the validator, so 304 survives and an admin's switch still moves the ETag. The seat flags it; the card chose the #23316 trade.
- **Dev:** opus under the quota-exhaustion exemption. spec / metadata-protocol / objectql / rest / runtime typecheck + tests exit 0; gates 119/119 run, 0 unmeasured (one `check:engine-double-contract --write` ledger entry, commit `7237921e`); ablation on the item-read serve line reds 5/11 new cases (item + cached), absence and list controls stay green. Pins flipped: `action-activation.test.ts`, `action-activation-dispatch.test.ts`, `api-action-forward.test.ts`, two dogfood tests (not run locally; CI's push battery answers), `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/api-backend.json` (rev 9 → 10). os-dev-report 6515747732.
- **Acceptance notes:**
  - `describeDisabledFlow` (`packages/services/service-automation/src/subflow-guards.ts:50`) still puts `sys_metadata_activation` and ADR-0126 §7.2 in the end-user `FLOW_DISABLED` message: the same lesson, the flow twin. Not this card (read only, not measured at a door); the seat routes it.
  - `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/platform-core.json` still says the data API is the only "what is off here" surface; after this PR the metadata read is one too. Same route.
- **Owed before any landing stroke:** the `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` review (`packages/spec/src/**` hunks) and the maintainer's approval of the key name; this seat cannot serve that tier now and hands the review over below.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `7237921e365096628921e03d89f7bc18d3cb9d85`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/objectql-engine.ts + packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-action-activation-reads.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts (getMetaItem, getMetaItems, getMetaItemCached), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-automation-flow-reads.ts (the seam template), packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-routes.ts (the cached object door), packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (getDisabledActions, describeDisabledAction), packages/objectql/src/action-activation.ts (ActionActivationProjection), packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts (hydrateActionActivations), packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts (getFlowRegistration), packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json, .changeset/27842-disabled-actions-beside-item.md, .changeset/27842-disabled-actions-served.md. Read, not reviewed; the rest of the diff is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT` (comment 6515763620).

Inputs: card #27842 (body, triage 6513025554, claim 6514354306, os-dev-report 6515747732), PR #27964 (body, 23-file list, net diff against `main` at this head), the check-runs on this head. The PR has since moved to `8216bec4`; this record judges `7237921e` alone and says nothing about the later head.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Public surface, `@objectstack/spec`.** Three optional keys named `disabledActions`: `string[]` on `GetMetaItemResponseSchema` (beside `item`, after `registration`) and on `GetMetaItemCachedResponseSchema` (beside `data`), `Record of objectName to string[]` on `GetMetaItemsResponseSchema` (beside `items`, after `registrations`). All `.optional()`, none defaulted, so an absent key parses as absent (pinned in `meta-item-response-shapes.test.ts`). Right: the card's Wanted 1 and 2, the `registration` / `registrations` template at L326 / L682 / L2318 on the base, taken one for one. The authorable-surface ledger gains exactly those three rows (`api/GetMetaItemResponse:disabledActions`, `api/GetMetaItemCachedResponse:disabledActions`, `api/GetMetaItemsResponse:disabledActions`); `content/docs/references/api/protocol.mdx` gains the two generated table rows. Right.
- **Public surface, `@objectstack/spec/contracts`.** `IObjectQLEngine.getDisabledActions?(): string[] | undefined`, optional, declared next to the action members. Right: the card's Wanted 3 asked for the `getFlowRegistration?` shape (`automation-service.ts:1381`) and left the carrying contract to the seat's measurement; the engine contract is where the activation projection lives and the slot the dispatch doors already resolve (`objectql`, registered by `ObjectQLPlugin` at `plugin.ts:719`). The first consumer probes it (`typeof read !== 'function'`, then `Array.isArray(answer)`), so the optional mark is honoured, not assumed.
- **Accept set.** Unchanged. No parse narrows: the stored object body is neither read for the key nor rewritten (`switchedOffActionsOf` reads `actions[].name` and returns names; `item.actions` is byte-identical with and without a ledger, pinned in three packages). The triage's ⛔ (no `visible` / `disabled` rewrite riding GET → PUT) holds in the tree. Right.
- **Faces.** Served face only; the execution face carries none (`audience === 'served'` on the list, `!execution` on the item read), and both draft returns of `getMetaItem` (`protocol.ts:10944`, `:11034`) exit before the key is computed, so the docblock's "absent on a draft read" is true of the code. A pending draft overlaid on the list gets no entry (`_draft === true` skipped). Right, and the same lines `registration` takes.
- **Absent versus `[]`.** `ObjectQL.getDisabledActions()` answers `undefined` while `ActionActivationProjection.durable` is false (no store attached) and `disabledNames()` otherwise; the seam turns a non-array into "no key". So absence = no `objectql` service, an engine without the member, or no ledger attached; `[]` = a ledger answered and no name in this object's `actions[]` is off. Right: the card reserved absence for "no ledger answered, never nothing is switched off", and `registration` makes the same split.
- **ETag / 304.** The protocol never hashes the key (it is read from the delegate `getMetaItem` after the hash) and refuses `notModified` when it is present; the REST cached door, which judges an object's 304 itself (`audienceFolds`), adds `!besideJudged` to the same condition and serves the unchanged ETag header. Right by the card's Wanted 1 (the #23316 trade, stated in the docblocks). Its cost is a ③ flag below.
- **Wire, the refusal.** 409 and the `ACTION_DISABLED` code are unchanged at both doors; the message string is the new plain sentence from the one producer (`ActionActivationProjection.describeDisabled`), and `disabledActionRefusal`'s no-sentence fallback is plain too. Every pin of the old sentence moved in one sweep (objectql, runtime, two dogfood tests, `api-backend.json` revision 9 → 10). Right by Wanted 4 and the triage's reading. The ledger table and ADR citation moved to one `info` log line in `ObjectQL.describeDisabledAction` — the lane's file, not a hit; see ③ for the gate it tripped.
- **`getMetaItemCached` return type** widened with `disabledActions?: string[]` beside `registration?`. Right.
- **Gate verdicts on this head** (the check-runs, read as they stood): `Check Changeset` success (both runs), `Governed Surface Queue Guard` success, `PR-body guards` success, `Lint · repo & tooling gates` success (carries `check:generated`, `check:api-surface`, `check:authorable-surface`), `Lint · CI, release & engine gates` success, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates` success, `Lint · ESLint` success, `Type Check · source gates` success, `Spec property liveness` success, `Dogfood Regression Gate` success, `Build Docs` success, `Flag docs affected by code changes` success. **`Lint · docs & code guards` FAILURE** (annotation: the `Error-code provenance guard` step, `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:error-code-provenance`, exit 1), so **`Lint & Repo Gates` FAILURE**. `Test Core`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger` were still in progress and `Build Core`, the eight `Test Core` shards, `Type Check UI` and `Build & E2E UI` were cancelled when the dev pushed `8216bec4`, so this head's gate roster is incomplete and red on one lane. The red lane's site is `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts` (the log line's metadata `{ action, code: 'ACTION_DISABLED' }`), outside `hits`; nothing in the two spec files is a stamp site. This head cannot land as it stands, whatever this record says about the contract.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/27842-disabled-actions-beside-item.md`: `@objectstack/spec` **minor**, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: added`. Right: three new optional response keys and one new optional contract member, nothing removed or narrowed; the authorable-surface ledger treats the response keys as surface rows, so `added` is the ledger's own word for them.
- `.changeset/27842-disabled-actions-served.md`: `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/runtime` **patch**, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: added`. The levels are the card's own prescription (Wanted 6: "metadata-protocol / rest / objectql patch") and the published change in each is an additive, optional widening (a wider `getMetaItemCached` return, a new `ObjectQL.getDisabledActions()`, a new sentence) — AGENTS.md's "a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships patch" covers that. What does not fit is the declaration line beside them: AGENTS.md says the level follows the kind alone and a kind other than `none` takes at least minor on a package the diff moves, and the flow twin's changeset (#23358, the template this PR cites) shipped **minor** on `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` and `@objectstack/service-automation` for the same shape (both changelogs list it under Minor Changes at 18.0.0). So the second changeset reads `added` on a patch bump, which the rule does not allow. **Should-fix**, one line either way: set `Metadata-protocol: none` on the consumer changeset (the key is spec's; these four packages add no authorable key of their own, and the card's patch stands), or raise the four to minor as #23358 did. `Check Changeset` is green on this head, so no gate holds it; the record does.
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` on the PR body and both changesets matches what the diff publishes. Right.
- No `skip-changeset`, no `!`, no narrowing arm, no ADR-0087 marker owed. Right.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Key name `disabledActions`** (card: the seat's measurement and its contract review; triage: "the maintainer approves the key in the PR"). The spelling is consistent across the three schemas, the contract docblock, the ledger, the generated docs, the seam and every test; it is the triage route's literal. This review does not approve a name the card reserved to the maintainer — **escalated**: the maintainer's word in the PR is still owed.
- **`[]` versus absent** (card: open). Answered above, ①: right, and stated in all three docblocks and the contract docblock in the same words.
- **The 304 trade on objects** (the seat's flag to this review, comment 6515763620; the dev's third out-of-scope finding). Answered: the card fixed it (Wanted 1, "never part of the ETag, so a read that carries it is never answered 304"), so the PR is right to do what it does, and the docblocks on `GetMetaItemResponseSchema` and `GetMetaItemCachedResponseSchema` say so. The cost is real and larger than the flow twin's: `PlatformObjectsPlugin` registers `sys_metadata_activation`, `ObjectQLPlugin` attaches the ledger on every such boot, so on a default deployment every cached `GET /meta/object/:name` answers 200 with the full body from now on, and objects are the console's hottest metadata read. The alternative the seat names — fold the switched-off names into the REST validator the way visibility, runtime-view, intake and audience fingerprints already are (`meta-item-read-routes.ts`, four nested `foldVisibilityFingerprintIntoEtag` calls) — is correct, keeps 304s, and moves the ETag on an administrator's switch. It is not this PR's to do; **escalated** to the maintainer beside the key-name approval, as a follow-up card if 304s on object reads are wanted back. No defect here.
- **Deviation 1, the log line lives in `ObjectQL.describeDisabledAction`.** Answered: the placement is sound (the one call both doors make on every refusal; `HttpDispatcher.deps.logger` is unwired), and the file is the lane's. But on this head that line is what `check:error-code-provenance` refused (①): a registered code in a non-test stamp-shaped position inside a package whose owner key does not list it. The guard's rule is a row under the stamping package's key or a recorded waiver naming the owner that holds the row; the next head's fix is not judged here, and its own record should confirm it answers that rule rather than the guard's spelling.
- **Deviation 2, no independent review was run.** This record is that review, for this head.
- **Deviation 4, the two dogfood tests were not run locally.** `Dogfood Regression Gate` ran green on this head. Answered.
- **Deviations 3 and 5** (PR footer; one `engine-double-contract.pinned.json` row for the new test's `findOne` double). Lane matters, not reviewed; the ledger row is the gate's own prescription.
- **Out-of-scope findings 1 and 2** (`platform-core.json` posture note now stale; `describeDisabledFlow` still names the ledger and ADR-0126 §7.2 in `FLOW_DISABLED`). Concur on both: the second is the same lesson on the flow twin and is its own card, since the automation checklist keys on that message. **Out-of-scope 4** (`HttpDispatcher` logger unwired): observation, concur.
- `open_questions`: none declared; none found.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts`** — judged against card #27842 (ruling 6512814276 letter B), the `registration` template on `main`, and the first consumer (`metadata-protocol`'s item, list and cached reads; `rest`'s cached object door).

Holds. Every claim the three docblocks make is true of the cited code: present only on an `object` read (`canonicalMetaType(type) !== 'object'` returns no reader, so `objects` is served and `view`, `flow`, `app` are not); `[]` only when a ledger answered (`durable` gate on the engine; the seam treats any non-array as absence); absent on a draft read (both draft returns exit first); beside `item` and never inside it (`item.actions` byte-identical, pinned); never in the ETag and never 304 when present (protocol and REST both). The list's "one entry per listed object that is not a pending draft" is `disabledActionsOf` line for line. The `string[]` element is the declarative action name, the same key the projection and the doors use, so a consumer can match it against `item.actions[].name` directly. Attempts to break it: a body with no `actions` array yields `[]` (a true statement — nothing of this object is off); a name switched off on another object is not named here (the per-object intersection, pinned with `some_other_objects_action`); a `?preview=draft` item read returns before the key (`:10944`); the execution face carries none; the plural type folds. One cost is accepted by the card, not by this file — the 304 trade in ③. **No must-fix. No should-fix in this file.**

**`packages/spec/src/contracts/objectql-engine.ts`** — judged against the card's Wanted 3, the `getFlowRegistration?` seam it names, and the first consumer (`protocol-action-activation-reads.ts`) plus the implementer (`ObjectQL`).

Holds. The member's two answers are kept apart in the type (`string[] | undefined`) and in the docblock, and the implementer honours both: `undefined` while no store is attached, the projection's names otherwise.
